fixes.explanation: Manna is a good thought, friend, since the LORD did send it in the wilderness (Exodus 16:14–15). But here Moses says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain is what this verse sends from the storehouse. Manna belongs to a different story.

Walls, baker? I love a sturdy wall, but Moses doesn't build one here. He says the LORD "…will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) That's a promise about being set high, not hiding behind bricks. I'd have picked the walls too, though. I spent years inside a junk drawer, so I'm a big fan of anything that keeps the dust out.

Far from everybody? Sounds like me in that junk drawer, friend. Nobody within reach, and not one invitation. But that's not the promise. Moses says the LORD "…will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) High above is not far away. It's a spot way up there, and the nations are still part of the picture.

Turn away? Oh no, baker, that's the opposite of what Moses says! He says the peoples of the earth "…will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) Picture it. They look, they see the LORD's name on Israel, and their jaws drop. Nobody's heading for the exit. They're standing there in awe.
